The room wants to be swept

The broom shakes the dust off

The barn became sparse after the clothes left  
The chamber decorated with woven fabrics

Surely she wanted some boys  
There is no money to count

The wallet falling apart

Ravens to be sewn in  
Crows to be shooed away  
The kerchief tied tight

Village girls mocked

Lying among the boys  
No woman laughed at me beautiful  
The girl teased playfully  
But the lazy woman laughed at me  
The girl teased badly  
They said I would remain without a husband  
Living without a partner  
I got a husband like a honey tree  
Got another like a German from Saaremaa  
I took him like a master's young man  
My groom was from Lake Peipus  
Dear man from Alutaguse  
Drinks from the lake's shore  
Drowns across the lake  
Dances beyond the lake  
Rode over the Finnish bridge  
Finnish bridge creaked  
The bottom beam cracked  
The hat flapped gently  
Village maidens watched  
If only that man were mine  
If only he were my partner far away  
Then he would ride along the road  
Gallop along the paths  
Horse below like the stove  
Head above like the moon  
Hat like the church bell  
Belt like the city flag ribbon  
Then he passed by, turned his head  
Lifted a nice hat  
Farewell, little maiden", "There, on the brass land,  
That big elder brother who always drinks,  
In one night, he finished a red garment all in tatters;  
He says nothing grown up.  
Window paper, please block the wind;  
I am the only family member here.

Carrying a rake,  
To the blue river like reed leaves,  
Let's go fishing,

Catch it, catch it,  
Catch a pair of pufferfish,  
Bring the pufferfish back home,  
Skewer it on a straw fire,  
Roast it over a hundred-mile fire and eat it.  
Twelve mountain ranges, I sleep alone,  
Spread out the quilt I used to sleep on in the big room,  
The worn curtain is pulled down,  
The quilt I used to cover is pulled down,  
Lying down asleep on the mat,  
Is my beloved here, is my beloved here?  
Neither my beloved nor sleep is here.  
In the upper room, the elder sister-in-law  
Says to arrange everything neatly;  
She only jabs with the big ladle and comes out.  
In the back room, the sister-in-law's child  
Says to arrange everything neatly;  
She takes the big ladle and comes out,  
Walking with a clattering sound.  
For us, elder siblings’ married life,  
How can we take a nap in the riverfront?  
Hurry, get out of bed,  
Make rice, make rice.  
I can't do it, I can't do it,  
No matter what, I just can't do it.  
At the village school, the green groom  
Half opens the big window,  
Then climbs inside,  
With a sturdy foot like a boss,  
Kicks this way but doesn't get up,  
Kicks that way but doesn't get up.  
Three times he kicks repeatedly,  
When I reached out my hand to his heart,  
There was no warm load,  
Only cold burdens,  
The window was opened suddenly,  
In the upper room, my mother,  
She brought that man’s magnet,  
And made a black rock soldier die, what is this story?  
Under us, plow the field,  
Take good care of the seedlings,  
That man’s magnet is unbearable,  
But his own magnet is acceptable.", "In Muan land, the golden maiden  
desired to be married.  
Soon after getting married,  
in the room where water liquor was made,  
she was told to spend the night.  
They lit a big charcoal fire,  
used the jade lamp for light,  
hung it over the bed,  
and placed a reed mat.

they placed a mat on the floor,

and conspired to kill.

looking out at some city,

With soybean paste soup like poison,  
stirred up and placed on the table,  
the water liquor single-layer blouse,  
worn very nicely and tightly,  
the water liquor black skirt,  
worn very nicely and tightly.  
At the mat stone floral seat,  
who would pair up and spread it?  
With the hair parted in two,  
swept beyond the comb lines,  
after taking a sip,  
all the four limbs loosen up.  
After two sips,  
the six thousand horses all collapse.

off they go and get tipsy.  
An older schoolmate who went to Seoul,  
like the Oe family’s elder,  
kicks off the Yangje side by foot,  
complaining about married life being tough.  
Why would she take a nap?  
In the inner chamber, parents say,  
she is the golden maiden, she is hers.  
Like a morning star, the chamber pot’s dignity,  
she is the golden maiden, she is hers.  
Half open the main hall door,  
tell mother to leave,  
tell father to leave,  
if the groom's mother-in-law knows,  
what kind of responsibility would she take?  
Plow the front field to buy servants,  
plow the back field to buy hired workers,  
manage the treatment of injuries well,

Name: 0_rice_mother law_household_wash
Representative_Docs:
['Laundry time, laundry time, laundry time at Ok Nang River.  
At the old wooden bridge, carrying laundry in a bamboo basket,  
Carrying pine tree laundry in the hand and heading to Ok Nang River,  
At Ok Nang River, scrubbing and washing the laundry.  

Suddenly, the washerwoman dances in front of me,  
Drifting, drifting, drifting in the clear water,  
Washing hands and feet in the clear water, offering the clean water,  
Not eating and leaving, after washing the black laundry and the clean laundry,  
The white laundry is washed white and comes back home.  

After only three days of laundry, the sound of happiness resonates,  
Feet swell, feet swell, the feet swell outside the house,  
The sound of happiness is shaking and the main gate clangs,  
Hearing that sound, the father opens the gate hurriedly,  
The twenty-five-year-old mourning man stands with his feet together.  

The front leader says, "Hurry up and come here,  
Bow once, bow," but no bow is made,  
Even after bowing three times, there is no reaction.  
The father says, "Son, son, my son,  
Come and bow, I will give you three thousand nyang,"  
But even after bowing three times, there is no response.  

The front leader says, "Bring your daughter in,"  
"Bring your daughter in."  
When the daughter is brought in and bows three times,  
Even the footprints fade. The mother says,  

"My daughter, my daughter, when I said go do laundry,  
Why did you go wash white cotton clothes and put on a white jacket,  
And hurry to go ahead,  
Please hurry up and wrap up. Oh, how frustrating, my fate is like this,  
Should I loosen my hair and lament that I saw the one I loved?  

When going over the nine hills, twisting and turning,  
After bowing on the ninth hill, entering home,  
Building a fence with nuruk (fermentation starter), making a fence with pine needles,  
Using thick needles, living for three years,  
Fingernails and toenails all fallen off after living for three years,  
Even hair has all fallen out, makeup is gone from the face,  
Why did my face turn yellow?', 'Three days after marriage, my sister-in-law, who picks cherries, urges me to weed the baby field.  
Look at the behavior of my mother-in-law.  
She washed her feet with cold water and urges me to weed the field.  
After weeding the first hill, then the second and third hills,  
it is almost lunchtime. As I arrive to have lunch,  
the sharp-tongued mother-in-law stirs her cold water feet.  
"Yesterday you came, my dear daughter-in-law, and today again, my dear daughter-in-law,  
what kind of work is this, coming only for lunch?"  
Hearing that voice, I was so overwhelmed that I couldn’t speak.  
Returning to my room, I tore seven pieces of cloth.  
I used two pieces to make a patchwork pouch, three pieces to make a bag,  
and one piece to make a simple sash, cutting and cutting,  
cutting my hair to look like a monk.  
I was going, but my husband said to go.  
He said he would ride a horse and go to the Seonbun family.  
Wearing half a plain sleeve, I turned around the side door.  
My husband said, "Dear, Shinjung family,  
don’t start any trouble with people.  
Dear, wearing half a plain sleeve,  
turn around the side door."  
At the end of his words, I suddenly grabbed his hand fiercely,  
trembling all over. "What’s wrong with you?  
What’s the matter with you, who usually wears a silk brocade waist bag?  
Why suddenly shave your head, who used to wear a golden hairpin and chop its hair?  
Why wear straw shoes over your worn shoes?  
Let’s go, let’s go back home."  
"I can’t go, I can’t go.  
Your parents' family is good, but I’m different, I have to go."  
Returning home, I asked my mother, "Where did he go?"  
"Since you left, he went away." The words made me so overwhelmed.  
Inside the three-foot coffin, inside the coffin, I cut my neck and died. / Sop'al', "Aga aga, Minul aga,  
They say it's a field, but it's all tangled up.  
Every little corner is covered with sesame,  
Seaweed is gathered on the hills.  
Each head is tied tightly,  
One bundle, two bundles,  
Even if you gather three bundles a day,  
All the officials have come and gone.  
But no one like Yone (a righteous man) appears.  
Aga aga, Minul aga,  
Step back, this path—  
They say it’s a matter of work.  
Looking for the right time and season,  
What is given as food  
Is three-year-old barley rice,  
Stuck to the bowl’s edge.  
What is given as the sauce  
Is three-year-old dinggi jang (fermented sauce).  
The plates are covered in dirt,  
And the spoons are just thrown away  
Ten or five ri (Korean miles) off,  
Twelve widths of cloth,  
One width torn into a cone hat,  
Eleven widths packed in a basket.  
Entering the bamboo grove,  
Leaning on the old fence,  
Mother and father, please receive my bow,  
I take my leave and step back.  
One watering turn passes, over a hundred seeds tremble,  
Two watering turns pass, all the dry corn trembles,  
Three watering turns and  
My husband who has gone to Seoul  
Holds a brush in his mouth,  
A book tucked at his side.  
My dear, my beloved,  
I am going, please don’t go.  
May my parents live a thousand years and ten thousand years,  
Leaving you behind, I find my way back to the temple.  
Master Jung, Master Jung,  
Is the place for poetry begging?  
Going to the place for poetry begging,  
Mother, please give a little alms.  
Though you do not give alms,  
My child’s face shows through,  
Like a newborn child—  
Not that word, please give a little more,  
Oh child, please give alms,  
Glutinous rice and millets are all done,  
Give a hand of millet alms,  
The bottomless sack receives the alms.  
Getting up, the fly falls,  
I slap with my hands in rejection.  
I slap with the gourd too,  
Filling a whole basket with that guy.  
Waiting for Aunt’s husband,  
He comes making steamed rice dishes,  
The bottomless sack, did you come for alms?  
Giving a fool’s gift, then leaving,  
As time passes and I come again,  
The household is ruined,  
In front of father-in-law’s rice storage,  
Pumpkin flowers are in abundance,  
In front of mother-in-law’s rice storage,  
Only withered flowers have bloomed.  
In front of Dongshi’s rice storage,  
Poison flowers bloom profusely,  
In front of sister-in-law’s rice storage,  
Cherry blossoms bloom profusely.  
On the husband’s mother’s place,  
Full blooms of cabbage flowers,  
Cabbage, oh cabbage,  
Looking at me, you bloom fully.  
Why do you bloom so fully?  
With that sound, the cabbage flower split apart,  
And entered the mountain alive."]

Name: 2_married life_marriage_married_husband

Mother-in-law is a chatterbox,

When I say let’s die, it’s youth,  
When I say to endure, it’s hardship,  
Even if I say I’m running away,  
Thinking of my parents,  
I can’t do either way.  
How am I supposed to live, how am I supposed to live?  
Oh, it’s frustrating, I can’t live like this.', "Brother, brother, cousin brother, how was married life like?  
Don't even mention married life, shaking my head at the straw-hat house.  
In a house with no shelter, shaking my head inside the small table,  
It's hard to keep fidelity. Married eyes are blind for three years,  
Deaf for three years,  
And dumb for three years.  
After living those three years,  
The three-layered front cloth becomes my hair,  
The rice-straw dance is all worn out,

how was married life in your in-laws' house?

['Hello links, hello falls,  
hello new doorposts,  
hello beam-like branches,  
hello little twig,  
hello thigh-dragging sedge,  
hello stove, give your hand,  
hello room, know me!  
May I come into the room,  
cause stirring at the threshold,  
tie the foal’s knots,  
make the stallion dance in the stable,  
perhaps you have springs here,  
linen cloths on the floor!  
Perhaps I water the cupboard’s corners,  
disturb the barn’s clothes,  
smooth ones of the linen folk!  
So let me say again,  
singing back again:  
If you have springs here,  
linen cloths on the floor,  
perhaps I water the cupboard’s corners,  
smooth ones of the linen folk,  
turn around the mill-wheel,  
rolling through the ears (of grain).', 'May one come indoors  
Or drive them outside?  
Blow this fire indoors,  
A warm fire down below,  
Perhaps the springs are flowing,  
Cloths on the floor?  
Maybe I’ll water the neckerchief,  
Ruin new felt boots?  
Yes, one may come indoors  
Or drive them outside.  
Do not sweep the floor  
Or damage the storage barn!  
People have lived here before,  
Drunk five, six shots of vodka,  
Eaten hundreds of loaves of bread,  
This is the front wall,  
Behind is the back wall.  
The drum comes indoors,  
An ass-wipe on the floor.  
Quietly, quietly, wisely, wisely,  
The Maldu people’s meeting.  
Perhaps a baby under the wing here  
A belt between thieves?  
There is no baby under the wing,  
No belt between thieves.  
Mother-in-law brought an awkward one on the road,  
There are two sets of twins, –  
I have no one or nothing!', 'Hello room, greeting in the room  
Hello barn, greeting in the barn  
May I come into the room  
To drive down the rows  
Do you perhaps have tobacco smoke in the room  
In front of the stove you have alder smoke  
Birch smoke in the chamber  
The mother-in-law hears, answers back  
You may come into the room  
To drive down the rows  
We do not have tobacco smoke in the room  
No willow smoke in front of the stove  
No alder smoke in front of the stove  
No birch smoke in the chamber  
Probably the smokes have gone from the room  
The vapors have gone through the window  
The soots between the branches. -  
You come into this room  
You drive the cattle to the barn  
You sit on the bench.  
You bring the horses to this yard  
You bring the oxen to this pole.  
The front goes to the first wall  
The back to the rear wall  
Lean against the tar bucket in the corner  
Dear stove, give room.  
Bring the small table, bring the fabric bolt  
Bring the oilcloth bag inside the room  
In front of the stove, the oil bag  
On the stove, the seed bag.  
The bride’s brother was a brother  
Be sure about Kerstu  
Choose the sister’s box  
Put a stone on Kerstu  
Put a ruble piece on the lock  
The other one to the other corner.  
Maiden, young girl  
Pull up the praise to Kerstu  
Start on the grain box  
What have you dipped your trowel in  
At twilight you have wriggled  
The millers have paid for it  
The flax workers have compensated  
Ellakene, brother  
No glove is made of stone  
Stockings do not sprout moss  
The belt does not sprout twigs  
Decorate the maiden if you can  
The horse shivers from the cold  
The saddle creaks  
Ellakene, brother  
If you gave time to grow  
Then give time to decorate  
I have no one to decorate me  
Nor a father to ask  
Village mothers decorate  
But old women prepare.']

Name: 8_heaven_dear mother_family_father mother
Representative_Docs:
['1. Greetings to you,  
That you have not forgotten us:  
The old and the young,  
Also the Holy God.  
2. Good day to this one,  
And to those in this house:  
The old and the young,  
Also the Holy God.', '1. Come down, God, from heaven,  
For we need You  
In our little yard  
To begin a little wedding.  
2. The father says:  
– May God bless!  
Bless, God,  
Both father and mother,  
To wreathe a garland  
For their child!  
3. The mother says:  
– May God bless!  
Bless, God,  
Both father and mother,  
To wreathe a garland  
For their child!  
4. The family says:  
– May God bless!  
Bless, God,  
Both father and mother,  
To wreathe a garland  
For their child!', '1. Be healthy,
My dear mother,
Did I not cook for you
Dinner early in the morning?

2. Did I not cook dinner,
Did I not bake bread?
What did I, dear mother,
Do to upset you so much?

3. Be healthy,
Holy icons,
I wiped you
Three times a week.

4. Be healthy,
Bright windows,
I wiped you
Until sunrise.

5. Be healthy,
Oak tables,
Where my suitors
Drank and ate.

6. Be healthy,
Pine thresholds,
Oh, where my white feet
Have walked.

7. Be healthy,
Yellow earth,
I anointed you
Early on Saturday.']

Name: 9_vodka_wine_drink_bring
Representative_Docs:
['Where is that uncle Joseph,  
Who brings the vodka?  
Let him bring it,  
So that we have enough.', '1. Vodka is flowing  
From under the shelf,  
Early, early,  
Vodka is flowing  
From under the shelf,  
Very early.  
2. Who will be  
The tavern keeper for that vodka?  
3. There will be a little tavern keeper,  
Sirozha, a young lad.  
4. He will keep the tavern,  
And serve the guests.', 'The walls moved,  
Like matchmakers they sat down,  
And they will move even more,  
When they get drunk on vodka.  
– Don’t move, walls,  
We haven’t sat long,  
We will drink the vodka  
And then go home.  
Alternative 2nd stanza:  
Do not groan...  
Honey-wine...  
We will go home.']

Name: 10_church_servant_maiden_dearest
Representative_Docs:
["I won't do it, I won't do it, I won't follow the women's trend  
Born a woman in heaven without any sin  
Distancing myself from my parents' intentions, before the age of twenty I entered the convent  
To extend my life, I visited other people's homes as if they were my own  
Making the intentions of others my own, pairing with virtuous people  
I envy, I envy, I envy the life of a man  
Born a woman in heaven without any sin  
I won't do it, I won't do it", "1. The priest from Losenice
preaches nicely,
hands out pictures,
binds hands.
2. I will also go
to that sermon,
to ask
for one picture.
3. The kind priest
from Losenice,
he gave me a picture,
and a living one.
4. Where shall I put that picture,
where shall I hide it,
when I have no
place for it.
5. If I put it in books,
it won't fit,
if I put it in a chest,
it will suffocate.
6. I will put it in the bed,
lie down next to it,
it will give me a kiss
and I will give it one too.", 'The local parish priest here preaches nicely, handing out pictures at the altar; I will also go to the sermon, I will ask for one picture. The local parish priest here: gracious, he gave me a picture, it is lively; where shall I, very sad, where shall I put it when I have no place for it anywhere! If I put it behind glass, it won’t fit; if I put it in the chest, it will get suffocated; I’ll put it behind the table, sit down by it: he will give me a kiss, and I him. From Klatovy. – Compare Suš. 474; Kol I, 241. If I put it behind glass, it will get cut; if I put it in the books, it won’t fit; I will put it in the bed under the blanket, I will enjoy it all winter.']

Name: 11_vodka_maiden_wedding_stove
Representative_Docs:
['1. Was the wedding mother somewhere around here?  
She promised to give vodka.  
She promised something sweet,  
But only gave something bitter.  
And she didn’t drink herself,  
And didn’t give us any.  

2. The matchmaker was good,  
But the female matchmaker was bad,  
She brewed vodka,  
But didn’t give us any.  

3. I crept, crept  
Along the hearth,  
Found a little hole,  
Drank the vodka,  
And didn’t drink myself,  
And didn’t give us any,  
Because she was cunning.', 'The matchmaker arrived at the matchmaker’s,  
Where shall we lay her down to sleep?  
If we lay her on the stove – it’s stuffy,  
If we lay her on the floor – it’s boring,  
We lay her on a blanket,  
And the matchmaker on the pile.  
Hold on, matchmaker, to the pile,  
So you won’t fall off your backside.', 'Oh, it’s strange to us, strange,  
That our matchmaker is not visible.  
Does she not have a coat?  
Is she borrowing boots?  
Or is she putting on galoshes?  
Or is she returning somewhere with an uncle?  
To this same melody:  
The matchmaker will stay overnight with the matchmaker,  
Where shall we lay her to sleep?  
We’ll lay her on the stove—it’s stuffy,  
We’ll lay her on the floor—it’s boring,  
We’ll lay her on the [boards],  
Let’s drink a little vodka.']

Name: 12_rice_husband_cousin_family
Representative_Docs:
["Seong-a, Seong-a, how was living in your husband’s home?  
Living in the husband's house was good, but it was difficult to place the handmade cloth on the round wooden frame.  
It was also hard to serve rice in the round watermelon-shaped bowl.  
It was hard to speak with the newly widowed uncle.  
Oh, how good it is, oh, how good it is, but I cannot do the farming.", 'Seong-a, Seong-a, cousin Seong-a, how was it living with your in-laws?  
Living with in-laws is good, but  
it’s hard to embroider such a small piece of cloth.  
It’s even difficult to speak about the widow’s clothing after the husband’s death.  
Hing-a, Hing-a, our Hing-a, how was it living with your in-laws?  
Where flowers used to bloom, no flowers bloom anymore.

Holding a drink, I climbed up Yeongnamnu in Miryang,  
Was it Yongdusan or Myungwol? By the Namcheon River, the clear wind and bright moon—endless clear wind and bright moon—  
I am now a person without a loved one. Oh, how nice, wonderful,  
What else is there to do but enjoy it?  
If it’s this good, I will have a daughter. Oh, how nice, wonderful.', "Brother Seong, cousin Seong,  
Do not worry just because I came out.  
If you set aside just one cup of rice,  
Seong's family can eat, and I can eat too.  
If the holiday water flows away,  
Is it Seong's matter or mine?  
If the rice crust goes away,  
Is it Seong's matter or mine?  
If the radish greens go away,  
Is it Seong's chicken or mine?  
Seong's house is in a prosperous village,  
They tie a crossbar with a protective rope.  
My house is in a poor village,  
We tie a protective rope with watercress.  
Seong's house is in a prosperous village,  
They build the fence with yeast cakes.  
My house is in a poor village,  
We build the fence with brass plates.  
Seong's house is prosperous,  
They hang ornaments on their ears.  
My house is poor,  
If I hang ornaments on my ears,  
When the southeast wind blows strongly,  
The sound of the ornaments is said to be even more pleasant.

>"]

Name: 13_dove_flowers_meadow_beloved
Representative_Docs:
['That hunter crawling gently in the pine grove over there,  
Do not catch that dove.  
The dove has lost its beloved like the day has lost the sun,  
Wandering all night long in search of its beloved.  
Do not catch it.', 'Where have you been flying, little dove, that you have worn your cheek, your beautiful feathers? "I have flown over the mountains, to my beloved, my darling, despite everything." If you fly again, I will catch you, my little dove. I will catch you by the barley ear: I will have you, my little dove, again soon. I will catch you by the rye ear, I will have you, my little dove, very soon. I will catch you among the flowers, I will have you, my little dove, in the nets. I will catch you on the beech tree, I will have you, my little dove, by the hand. I will have you by the hand: I will not let you go, my little dove, for a year. I will have you with both hands: I will not let you go, my little dove, until the grave.', 'Our rooster crows, crows, it will be early morning: my Jeníček is thinking, thinking of me, madam! If only it were possible for you to give my joy a little kiss! Madam, get up, get up, master is calling you; prepare breakfast, prepare it, there will be a wedding at our place: I will be getting married, I must get up early in the morning, early morning. My Jeníček is coming to us, coming to us, from over by the grove; truly, I know him well, know him well, with his black horse: just hurry up a lot, my joy, I’m glad to see you. Glad of that, I am glad, I am glad, my heart is jumping; my intention pleased, pleased, for you, my boy: I will not be afraid that I have to sleep alone all by myself.']

Name: 14_dance_apron_young girl_beautifully
Representative_Docs:
["Dance, dance, little maiden  
Dance, dance, I am watching  
Is your apron fitting  
Or is the headdress flat  
Maybe there are babies under your wing  
Dung flies under the apron  
But I am dancing, why don't you dance  
Over the crossbeam, over the table  
Over six devil’s heads  
Over seven log walls  
The midwife has babies under her wing  
Dung flies under the apron.", 'Eat dips, drink dips  
Don’t hide dips in your pocket  
I am careful in seeking  
Clever in feeling pockets  
I feel under your fur coat  
I look for a new coat inside.  
Dress up, dress up, young girl,  
Dress quickly, hasten quickly  
Hasten to the hundred ride  
You will get to dance down  
Spokes clattering  
The sled is ready, the groom is ready  
Dress quickly, young girl  
The horse is already shod with iron  
The bridles’ heads are braided  
The reins’ breasts are already braided  
The reins’ necks are already braided  
The reins’ ears are already jingling  
The reins’ eyes are already silky  
The reins’ eyebrows are golden.', 'Blow the pipe, little Peebu,  
Play the horn, Saxon.  
I am coming to dance the oak,  
To make young spruces sway.  
I dance, the fence rumbles,  
The spruce room resounds,  
The flagstone floor clatters,  
Feet want to dance,  
The room wants new clearing;  
The floor wants stomping,  
The wallsides want stepping.  
Dance, dance, Lutsu Mari.  
Do your feet work right away,  
Do handfuls of steps go through.  
Is the envelope round,  
Is the fabric half-length,  
Or are the little ones under wings,  
The rascals between belts.  
Slowly, slowly, wisely, wisely,  
Gently dance, young lady,  
Step beautifully.  
So the apron strings don’t snap  
Nor the too tight shoe straps.']

I must not, my dear, disappear  
Do not swear by the people's year  
By better days  
I leave this place to you  
I give my seat to others  
I push the door to another  
Let me come tomorrow to try  
Let me come to see  
The patch is where I left  
The chair is where I lifted  
The bench is where I held  
The room to sweep with brooms  
The stove to start with sticks  
The chip cries like a whisker.", 'I walked around it three times, tadyadyadum – walked around, but I never found where my beloved lies. Name: 16_maiden_groom_young lad_servant
Representative_Docs:
['A young virgin girl,  
A little bird with flaxen hair,  
You think of beauty without a husband,  
A white girl without a husband,  
You think of pure boys without a husband,  
You think of bashful men without a husband.  
You are not beautiful without a husband,  
Not a white bride without a husband,  
Nor a pure boy without a husband,  
You are strange without a husband,  
A thief without a husband,  
Half a girl without a boy,  
A fat woman without men.  
The young maiden understood and said,  
"There is no pot for me to pee in,  
No corner for me to let go,  
I would give boys a chance to sniff,  
Young men to take a whiff,  
And old maids to envy.  
Are you not pure without a boy,  
Are you not a white bride either,  
Are you not beautiful at all,  
Or are you clever in some way?"', "Oh, you sawmill attendants  
Wedding guests on the groom's side  
Why are you standing here  
He has long since gone away from here  
In Paide, he shaved his head  
Asked for his shoes to be laced  
Had a wedding in Petersburg  
A dowry was arranged in Tallinn  
The groom’s beard has certainly been washed here  
The bridegroom’s beard has been washed  
The master’s vessel has been cleaned  
We shall see  
Whether the groom’s beard has been washed here  
Whether the master’s dagger has been cleaned  
Young maiden  
Why do you listen in the chamber  
Standing by the walls  
Among the weak ones  
Come inside, my acquaintance  
Take to the woods, my acquaintance  
A big greeting to you, my love  
Take strangers as your own  
Leave your own as strangers  
Young maiden  
I do not come to eat out of hunger  
Nor to drink wine  
I came because of stories  
I came to do beauty  
Women’s fun  
I came to receive a full measure  
I come to gather skulls  
A full measure for my brother's shoulders  
So let me tell again  
Let me sing back again  
Dear one, brother dear  
Do not curse me  
Swear by the holy angels  
Do not curse the girls’ fathers,  
Do not curse the girls’ mothers  
Swear by the old women,  
Who made the girls tall  
Tall and dear  
Before I had forty girls  
With me I had eighty  
Weddings worth half a thousand  
Now you have forty girls  
But not eighty with you  
Weddings worth half a thousand.", "Hello, dear grown men,  
Come, let us get to know each other,  
Let us accept the greeting,  
Let us give a hand to the guest,  
Let us bow in respect.  
Hello father-in-law, as the master,  
Hello mother-in-law, as the lady,  
Hello on the way when coming in,  
In the turn of the path,  
Who greets you on the road  
Will give you a hand in return.  
Do not forbid the engaged,  
Do not separate the married,  
Who had placed a pair of rings,  
Announced by the church leader,  
Wearing a black robe.  
Young lad, little boy,  
Already from here he has gone.  
He struck his mark into the turf,  
On the crossway of Riga road,  
He struck a piece into the clouds,  
He has spent nights awake,  
Sharing gifts in Aru village,  
Turning heads in Seidla.  
He has gone away to the city,  
Sent to Tallinn as a servant.  
Young lad, little boy,  
If you want to chase after him,  
Take the mark from the turf's edge,  
From the crossway of Riga road,  
Take a piece from the clouds,  
Chase after him with a gray horse,  
Rush with a fast horse,  
Catch him at Võigula."]

Name: 17_braid_hair_tears_mother
Representative_Docs:
['1. On Saturday, on a little Saturday,  
A mother calls her daughter:  
2. – Come, come, daughter, to the house,  
It’s time to braid your hair.  
3. The daughter comes, crying loudly:  
– Have I bothered you?  
4. – You, my daughter, have not bothered me,  
But your hair is no longer yours,  
5. The time from God has come,  
For you, daughter, to get married.', "1. I will cross the house and the hallway,  
I will fall to my mother's knees:  
2. – So, mother, smooth down my head  
And comb my fair hair.  
3. But first, mother, you braided me,  
You tied me up somehow.  
4. And now you are unbraiding me,  
Shedding small tears.", '1. Oh, my aunt was combing me,  
She did not smooth my little curls,  
2. Oh, she combed me with a comb,  
Stuck a rose flower in my hair.  
3. And my mother was watching,  
Washing her face with tears.  
4. Look, mother, at my place,  
All the girls are sitting with braids.  
5. But I combed my own,  
Because dew fell on mine.  
6. Dew fell from the white blossom  
From today and forevermore.']

Name: 18_family_wealth_coming_rich
Representative_Docs:
['Where did you know to come to us from?  
Did you know over the hills,  
Did you know over the mountains?  
From our great swamp,  
From the land of the people of Rahakaid,  
From the old farm of the taalders,  
From the old family of the penings.  
- Where did we know to come to you,  
We knew over the hills,  
We knew over the mountains,  
We heard the rustle of legs,  
The rustling of skins,  
At the smell of sourness.', '1. Oh, I will stand on the log,  
Waiting for the whole family.  
2. Come together, dear family,  
Both poor and rich.  
3. Poor and rich,  
Far and near.  
4. The rich ride on horses,  
The poor go on foot.  
5. The poor greet,  
The rich scold.', 'Little boy, little lad,  
How did you know to come to us,  
To us, the great family,  
Dear to wealth, dear to riches?  
Because I knew to come to you,  
To you, the great family,  
Dear to wealth, dear to riches:  
I heard the rustling of cups,  
The tapping of leather horns,  
I heard cups coughing,  
Leather horns snapping.']
